questions.stem: Which separation technique would be most suitable for separating sand from water?
questions.explanation: Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. Sand does not dissolve in water, so it can be trapped in filter paper while the water passes through.

questions.stem: How would you obtain pure water from a salt water solution?
questions.explanation: Simple distillation heats the solution so the water evaporates, then condenses and is collected as pure water. Evaporation would give the salt, not the water. Filtration cannot separate dissolved substances.

options.text: Separating dissolved substances based on their different solubilities
Separating magnetic materials from non-magnetic ones

questions.explanation: Chromatography separates dissolved substances by their different solubilities in a solvent. Substances that are more soluble travel further up the paper.

questions.stem: Which technique separates two miscible liquids with different boiling points?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids with different boiling points. The liquid with the lower boiling point evaporates first and is collected separately.

questions.stem: To obtain salt crystals from a salt solution, which method would you use?
questions.explanation: Evaporation or crystallisation can be used to obtain dissolved solid from a solution. The water evaporates, leaving behind the salt crystals.

questions.stem: In simple distillation, what is the purpose of the condenser?

options.text: To heat the liquid to boiling
To cool the vapour back into a liquid

questions.explanation: The condenser cools the vapour (gas) back into a liquid, which is then collected. Cold water flows around the condenser tube to remove heat from the vapour.

questions.stem: A mixture contains iron filings and sulfur powder. Which method would be most effective for separating them?
questions.explanation: A magnet can separate iron filings from sulfur because iron is magnetic and sulfur is not. This uses the different physical properties of the two substances.
